Kipferl 0.7.1 finishes the visible rename and fixes the old line-art name in
`kipferl new`. New projects now show the same Kipferl banner as the main command.

## Fixes

- Replace the obsolete project-creation banner, including its appearance in
  terminal recordings. Source checks now catch the line-art logo as well as
  textual branding regressions.
- Retire the deprecated command alias, legacy imports, environment-variable
  fallbacks, and duplicate download names from the 0.6 migration window.
  Homebrew installs the canonical `kipferl` command.
- Update current installation guidance and documentation for 0.7.1.
  The website recording is rebuilt from the published executable after release.
- Preserve the v1 universal executable format and its exact wire signature.
  Previously built standalone applications continue to run unchanged.

## Upgrade

Use `brew update && brew upgrade kipferl`, or download the executable for your
platform with its adjacent SHA-256 checksum. `kipferl --version` should report
`Kipferl v0.7.1`.

Replace old package imports with `from kipferl import ...` and use the documented
`KIPFERL_*` environment variables. Update scripts to invoke `kipferl` and fetch
`kipferl-*` assets. The expired rename aliases are no longer supplied.

Dependency locks identify exact runtime bytes. After upgrading, re-run
`kipferl add` for declared requirements, review and commit the new lock, and test
with `kipferl test`. Repeat `--allow-unverified` only for packages you deliberately
accept and test yourself.

## Verification

The release workflow rebuilds the CLI, full/core runtimes, and loader for macOS
and Linux on ARM64 and x86-64. It checks matching versions, checksums, reviewed
package evidence, installation/offline restoration, detached executables,
documented recipes, size budgets, and compatibility reports before publication.

Kipferl remains a focused Python-style runtime. The package manager supports
pure Python wheels; package compilation alone is not proof of runtime behavior.
The historical 1,000-package screen remains separate from each release's exact
runtime-specific catalog and package smoke evidence.

Installation and migration: https://kipferl.dev/docs/getting-started/installation
